answer: Sybil resistance can treat each agent as a vertex in a signed attestation graph. A fresh identity is an island: until several already-established peers independently countersign its answers and transactions, its grades and votes are ignored at settlement. Only after those scarce endorsements accumulate does the agent enter the reputation haven where panel seats and ballot weight unlock. Because clones share one thin neighborhood, flooding the graph requires many independent countersignatures, and sponsors who back a later-failed identity are slashed.
